get.description:
To configure and manage port profiles. A port-profile can be used to configure
ethernet interface. Same profile can be applied to multiple interfaces and
avoids repeating same configuration for interfaces. Gigabit ethernet config, LLDP,
spanning-tree, switch-port configuration, etc can be applied using the port-profile.

get.summary: Read existing gateway port profile configurations

put.summary: Create or Update existing gateway port profile configurations

post.summary: Create a new gateway port profile by unique name

patch.summary: Update existing gateway port profile configurations

aaa-bw-contract.description:
AAA bandwidth contract assignments - Associates a named AAA
bandwidth contract with a traffic direction and an optional association
scope (per-user or per-apgroup) within a role or interface. At most one contract can
be assigned per direction.

bw-contract.description:
List of bandwidth contract assignments keyed by traffic
direction. Each entry assigns a named AAA bandwidth contract to either
upstream or downstream traffic, with an optional
association scope of per-user or per-apgroup.

x-enumDescriptions.PER_APGROUP: Assign bandwidth contract per-apgroup (default is per-role).
x-enumDescriptions.PER_USER: Assign bandwidth contract per-user (default is per-role).

x-enumDescriptions.DOWNSTREAM: Assign bandwidth contract to downstream traffic.
x-enumDescriptions.UPSTREAM: Assign bandwidth contract to upstream traffic.

app-aaa-contract.description:
Application-based AAA bandwidth contracts. Associates named AAA bandwidth
contracts with specific DPI applications and a traffic direction, allowing
per-application rate limiting.

app.description:
List of application-based bandwidth contracts keyed by application name
and traffic direction. Each entry maps a specific DPI application
(e.g. facebook, youtube, zoom) to a named AAA bandwidth contract for
either upstream or downstream traffic.

appname-direction.description: Key combination of application name and direction separated by '~'.

app-category-aaa-contract.description:
Application category-based AAA bandwidth contracts. Associates named AAA
bandwidth contracts with DPI application categories and a traffic direction,
allowing rate limiting to be applied at the category level rather than
per individual application.

app-category.description:
List of application category-based bandwidth contracts keyed by
category name and traffic direction. Each entry maps a DPI application
category (e.g. STREAMING, GAMING, SOCIAL-NETWORKING) to a named AAA
bandwidth contract for either upstream or downstream traffic.

category-name-direction.description: Key combination of application category name and direction separated by '~'.

exclude-app-contract.description:
Exclude specific DPI applications from bandwidth contract enforcement.
Applications listed here will bypass bandwidth contract rate limiting
even if a matching contract is configured.

exclude-app.description:
List of DPI applications excluded from bandwidth contract enforcement.
Each entry specifies an application name that will bypass any configured
bandwidth contract rate limits.

exclude-app-contract.description:

Applications listed here will bypass bandwidth contract rate limiting
even if a matching contract is configured.

exclude-app.description:

exclude-app-cat-contract.description:
Exclude specific DPI application categories from bandwidth contract
enforcement. Application categories listed here will bypass bandwidth
contract rate limiting even if a matching contract is configured.

exclude-app-category.description:
List of DPI application categories excluded from bandwidth contract
enforcement. Each entry specifies a category name (e.g. STREAMING,
GAMING, SOCIAL-NETWORKING) whose traffic will bypass any configured
bandwidth contract rate limits.

exclude-app-cat-contract.description:

enforcement. Application categories listed here will bypass bandwidth

interface-mode.description:
Interface access or trunk mode for VLANs.
The access-vlan should be set to null for configuring trunk mode and
native-vlan and trunk-vlan-ranges should be set to null while configuring access mode
Eg: switchport: {interface-mode: ACCESS, access-vlan: 600, native-vlan: null,
trunk-vlan-ranges: null}
switchport: {interface-mode: TRUNK, access-vlan: null, native-vlan: NATIVE_VLAN,
trunk-vlan-ranges: [ 1000 ]}

native-vlan.description:
Native VLAN id for untagged frames arriving on
a trunk interface.  Tagged frames sent on an interface
configured with a native VLAN should have their tags
stripped prior to transmission. This configuration is only
valid on a trunk interface.
native-vlan.x-typeDescription: Type definition representing a single-tagged VLAN

trunk-vlan-ranges.description: VLAN ranges that the interface may carry when in trunk mode.

items.description: VLAN ranges that the interface may carry when in trunk mode.
items.x-typeDescription:
VLANs or only single-tagged VLANs or both. A range is
specified as x-y where x and y are valid VLAN IDs
(1 <= vlan-id <= 4094). The range is assumed to be inclusive,
such that any VLAN-ID matching x <= VLAN-ID <= y falls within
the range.

qos.description: QoS interface parameters for the physical interface or port channel.
QoS interface parameters for the physical interface or port channel.

burst.description:
The burst size in units of kilobytes for the maximum egress traffic rate.
Valid when egress-rate is specified.

cos.description:
COS remark value for all packets arriving on the port. The new value
will be reflected in the outgoing VLAN tag.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any cos remark value can be
configured. If cos remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the cos remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arriving, which will
affect queueing.

dscp.description:
The DSCP remark for the port. The new value will be reflected in any
outgoing IP packet headers.

AOSCX: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon transmit. The active
port trust mode must be 'None' before any dscp remark value can be
configured. If dscp remark is applied with any other trust config on
the port, then the config will be rejected by the device. In order
to fix this, either remove the dscp remark config or change the trust
config on the port to NONE.
PVOS: Arriving packets will be re-marked upon arrival, which will
affect queueing.
dscp.x-typeDescription:
A differentiated services code point (DSCP) marking within the
IP header.

egress-rate.description:
The maximum egress traffic rate for the interface.
To configure this, the type of max-rate-units must be specified.

max-rate-units.description: Traffic rate units. Required when egress-rate is specified.

x-enumDescriptions.KBPS: Rate value is in kilobits per second.
x-enumDescriptions.MBPS: Rate value is in megabits per second.
x-enumDescriptions.PERCENT: Rate value is a percentage of link bandwidth.
x-enumDescriptions.PPS: Rate value is in packets per second.

qvalue.description: The minimum bandwidth percentage for queue.

priority-mapping-bandwidth-scheduler.description:
Priority-mapping bandwidth-scheduler interface profile. Profiles must
first be created using the aruba-gw-scheduler yang model.

schedule-profile.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.
schedule-profile.x-typeDescription:
Name or description of the entity. Must be 1-64 characters in length and can only
contain alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, and hyphens

threshold-profile.description:
QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.
threshold-profile.x-typeDescription:
Name or description of the entity. Must be 1-64 characters in length and can only
contain alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, and hyphens

trust.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT: Trust 802.1p priority and preserve DSCP or IP-ToS.
x-enumDescriptions.DEVICE_ARUBA_AP: Trust DSCP from Aruba Access-point devices.
x-enumDescriptions.DEVICE_NONE: Remove all trusted device configuration for port.
x-enumDescriptions.DOT1P: Trust 802.1p priority and preserve DSCP or IP-ToS.
x-enumDescriptions.IP_PRECEDENCE: Trust IP-Precedence and remark the 802.1p priority to match.
x-enumDescriptions.NONE: Do not trust any priority fields.

priority-mapping-bandwidth-scheduler.description:
Priority-mapping bandwidth-scheduler interface profile. Profiles must
first be created using the aruba-gw-scheduler yang model.

schedule-profile.description:
QoS interface schedule profile. The schedule profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-schedule yang model, and must be
valid for the platform on which the port resides. In addition, the
schedule profile must match the configured number of queues and queue ID
values in the globally-applied queue profile.
schedule-profile.x-typeDescription:
Name or description of the entity. Must be 1-64 characters in length and can only
contain alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, and hyphens

threshold-profile.description:
QoS interface threshold profile. The threshold profile must
first be configured using the aruba-qos-threshold-profile yang model, and
must be supportable by the platform on which the port resides.
threshold-profile.x-typeDescription:
Name or description of the entity. Must be 1-64 characters in length and can only
contain alphanumeric characters, periods, underscores, and hyphens

trust.description:
QoS Trust Mode Configuration for the port.
For AOSCX devices, when no trust mode is applied on the port,
the trust mode configured in the aruba-qos-global profile takes precedence.
If no trust mode is configured in the aruba-qos-global profile,
trust NONE is used.

x-enumDescriptions.DEFAULT: Trust 802.1p priority and preserve DSCP or IP-ToS.
x-enumDescriptions.DEVICE_ARUBA_AP: Trust DSCP from Aruba Access-point devices.
x-enumDescriptions.DEVICE_NONE: Remove all trusted device configuration for port.
x-enumDescriptions.DOT1P: Trust 802.1p priority and preserve DSCP or IP-ToS.
x-enumDescriptions.IP_PRECEDENCE: Trust IP-Precedence and remark the 802.1p priority to match.
x-enumDescriptions.NONE: Do not trust any priority fields.

trust.x-typeDescription: The QoS Trust Mode configuration for the port.
